objective: A classification fixed in advance, computed exactly. For every ordered pair of creative lines in the 32 three-fold spaces up to 22 points and in trees of Fano atoms up to 25 points, compare the native relation (mutual, one-way, silent) with the pair's place in the tight-cut decomposition: the same atom; adjacent atoms, with the cut's direction and each line's role at the cut; atoms farther apart, with the directions along the path; glue braces. Predict that the native relation is a function of that place. From the dictionary, fix a reconstruction of the atoms and of the cut directions.
status: Proved by BRACE-TREE-20261105-001B-P001 (exact computation on 50 spaces): the native relation between two atom lines is a function of their place in the tight-cut decomposition wherever the atoms are the same, adjacent or joined through atoms only (21 places, 10,074 pairs), and can depend on more through plane glue; plane glue is silent unless a non-Fano handle lies between; all 50 cuts between two atoms are read in their direction; the source rule fixed here counts the Heawood braces, and the genus, on all 47 spaces without a non-Fano brace
title: The brace dictionary
